notes.title: "The Northern Path" Demo Release
notes.notes:
Ready to take your first steps along The Northern Path?
On February 24, 2025, we’ll be launching a demo version of The Northern Path as part of Steam Next Fest!

[h3]What can you expect in the demo?[/h3]
[list]
[*]The first in-game location: unique quests and an introduction to key characters who will set the tone for your entire adventure.
[*]Sled dogs: try out the sled mechanics and see how different dogs affect its handling.
[*]Snowy landscapes and local mysticism: immerse yourself in the beauty of northern scenery and learn about the culture of the Yakutpeople.
[/list]
[h3]Final Release[/h3]
The full version of the game will be available right after the festival ends. The release version of The Northern Path will include:
[list]
[*]The continuation of the story, featuring new locations and characters;
[*]Expanded exploration and sled team progression;
[*]Controller support
[/list]
[h3]Support Us![/h3]
[list]
[*]Add the game to your wishlist so you won’t miss any updates and will be notified as soon as the demo goes live.
[*]Follow the news: we’ll soon share more details about the festival, new features, and our development plans.
[*]Share your impressions and feedback in the comments, so we can make  The Northern Path even better for you!
[/list]

See you soon at Steam Next Fest!

notes.title: “The Northern Path”: From Conception to Reality
notes.notes:
[h3]Sources of Inspiration[/h3]
When choosing the setting for our game, we were captivated by the unique culture of the  Yakut, their mythology deeply intertwined with nature, their faith in spirits and deities permeating every aspect of their  lives.  Here is how we conveyed it in our game and introduced the players to their culture:
[list]
[*] Spirits and gods. The game’s narrative features dangerous spirits — abasy, icchi, ghosts of the past, and powerful deities, all of them impacting the protagonist’s fate.
[*] National symbols in design. From the user interface to entire settlements, our game strives to reflect the patterns and motifs characteristic of northern Yakutia.
[*] Distinctive characters. Players will meet an olonkhosut (epic storyteller), a shaman, hunters, and other unique locals. 
[*] Authentic regional fauna. The types of animals and fish you can encounter — or hunt and fish for — are based on real fauna of the Yakut region.
[*] Specialized tools. We introduced the kuyuur, a traditional instrument for lake fishing. As you progress, you’ll also discover other everyday items used by the Yakut people.
[*] Visuals of key characters. When designing the looks of our characters, we combined realistic historical details (clothing, gear) with elements of Yakut tradition.
[/list]

[i]Early In-Game Effect Concept:[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45367206/f09f1bbd5fe94ec57f9ff53d7b81371aa8fa89f6.png[/img]

[h3]Real Historical Roots[/h3] 
While developing the storyline, we became intrigued by the story of Pyotr Fyodorovich Anjou, a navigator and polar explorer who made a significant contribution to the exploration of the Northern Sea Route. Parts of his biography formed the basis of our game’s plot: in 1821, he set out on an expedition to find the legendary Sannikov Land, which he also references in the game’s story.
As you play, you’ll also uncover details about local settlements and real historical events, recording them in your personal journal.

[i]Early Character Concept:[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45367206/421c4f01ed141fbc1340e7c8931b0eaf87589baf.png[/img]
 
[h3]Early Stages of Development[/h3] 

[b]World Map: Openness or Sequence?[/b]
From the outset, we aimed to create vast northern locales and faced a central question: should we allow the player to roam freely from the start (a fully open world), or introduce stricter narrative constraints?
Ultimately, we decided to preserve freedom of movement. Want to head to Kotelny Island from your very first hours of play? Go for it! But be prepared for tough challenges if your dog sled team isn’t sufficiently upgraded yet. At the same time, the story unfolds in a sequential manner so the narrative atmosphere remains coherent and immersive.

[i]Early Map Concept:[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45367206/5d932f11e26d0a07590eebd76152bf1f62d5e352.png[/img]

[b]Sled Dogs — More Than Just Part of a Team![/b]
We devoted special attention to choosing sled dog breeds, aiming to include real ones (even some now extinct, like the Gilyak Laika). It was important to us that these dogs weren’t just an extra feature. In the end, some of them became fully-fledged characters with their own personalities and backstories.
Another task was designing the management of the sled team: we went through multiple iterations, refining the controls and tweaking how dogs react to obstacles, so they can’t dash off a cliff. The dogs can subtly adjust the sled’s direction if you drive too close to an edge. As a result, handling the sled feels both realistic and enjoyable.

[b]Snow Everywhere![/b]
“The Northern Path” is set against the backdrop of the Arctic, so the look and feel of snow is especially important.
During prototyping, one of the critical questions was whether to keep dynamic snow physics, allowing the sled and each dog to leave realistic tracks. In the end, we decided against it.
The reason was simple: we wanted to focus on smooth gameplay across large expanses, without overburdening the system.
After testing various approaches, we settled on a uniform snowy surface — atmospheric and pleasing to the eye — where points of interest stand out clearly.

[i]Early Snow Versions:[/i] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45367206/b615d2b9046d738b19c9d3b273e985742204d3a2.png[/img]

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
Thus, step by step, the vision for “Northern Path” took shape: from the rich legends of the Yakut people and Anjou’s historical background to practical considerations in game design and optimization.
Thank you for keeping up with our updates! If you have questions or suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments. Your feedback helps us make the game even better!

notes.title: Begin Your Journey in "The Northern Path"!
notes.notes:
[b]The Northern Path – Brave the Secrets of the Polar Frontier![/b]
The year is 1823. Here, in northern Yakutia, time flows differently. Days are filled with cheerful chores, the barking of sled dogs, and sparkling snow, while nights brim with hidden untold stories.
You are Nikolay Trofimov, a young officer who has traveled to the world’s edge in search of his missing father.
Get ready to discover an exciting frozen realm, delve into the traditions of local peoples, and find fresh adventures and new friends. We welcome you on your Northern Path!

[b]The Soul of Winter[/b]
[list]
[*] Survive and explore: hunt, fish, gather resources, and upgrade your sled so it never fails you on the trail.
[*] Discover the culture of Yakutia’s peoples: learn about their customs, talk to the keepers of ancient lore, and feel the warmth of legends about gods and mortals, about mysteries both past and present.
[*] Feel the breath of mystery: follow the call of the unknown, the beat of the shaman’s drum, and the whispers of spirits—they might lead you to unexpected revelations.
[*] Assemble a legendary sled dog team: cheerful leader Dobor and other faithful dogs will guide you across endless snowy horizons.
[*] Venture into the night, both daunting and alluring: certain secrets only reveal themselves under a star-filled sky. Yet darkness can draw your mind too far into the spirit world... and that means trouble.
[/list]
[b]Support Our Journey[/b]
We’re a small indie team obsessed with the beauty of Russia’s Far North and the cultures of Yakutia. Our goal is to share the magic of this unique world with you. 
Very soon, we’ll be showcasing the demo version of Northern Path at the Steam Next Fest!

[b]Join Our Adventure:[/b]
[list]
[*] Add the game to your wishlist to be the first to know about the demo and future updates.
[*] Follow our news: we have stories about the secrets of the tundra, historical references—and, of course, sled dogs!
[*] Share your questions and ideas—we’ll be happy to talk about the aspects of our game, northern legends, and more.
[*] Get ready to hear a thousand tales of the Far North—then add your own story to the mix. We’ll be waiting for you on the path!
[/list]
